title: Smells Like Teen Spirit: chords and your first sharp

blocks.text:
Nirvana's song: big held chords in the left hand and a syncopated riff in the right, with a black key in it.

**By the end** you can play the left hand's chords and the right hand's riff, each alone.

blocks.caption: Smells Like Teen Spirit, a piano arrangement (PDMX), bars 3–9. ▶ to hear it.

blocks.text:
# Two chords
The left hand holds a chord for each whole bar: **E minor** (E G B) and **C** (C E G), one after the other. They're the triad shape from last lesson, fingers 5 3 1: from E minor, move the whole hand down to C.

blocks.title: E minor and C, by name
The chords, left hand
blocks.about: Wait for me, left hand, bars 4–9.

blocks.text:
# Your first sharp
The sign at the start of each staff, **♯** on an F line, is a **key signature**: every F in the piece is played as **F sharp**, the black key just right of F. The riff uses it: its notes are F♯, G, A, B, C, D and E.

blocks.caption: F, F sharp and G: F sharp is the black key between them.

blocks.title: G to E on the staff
blocks.about: Twenty cards (the white keys; F sharp you add by the key signature).
blocks.doneWhen: 16 of the 20 cards clean in one set

blocks.text:
# Syncopation
The riff's notes often start on the "and", between beats, and are **tied** (a curve joining two notes) over the next beat: you play once and hold through. That off-beat push is **syncopation**. Play its rhythm first, on any key.

blocks.title: The riff's rhythm
blocks.doneWhen: 80% of the notes on time in one run

blocks.title: The riff, right hand
blocks.about: Wait for me, right hand, bars 3–6.

blocks.text:
# G position
With one sharp, F♯, this song is in the world of **G major**. Its riff's middle, **G A B C D**, is **G position**: right thumb on the G above middle C, one finger a key up to D. (The riff also reaches down to F♯ and up to E.) The left hand's G position: little finger on the G on the bass staff's bottom line, thumb on D.

Made-up tunes in G position, fresh every card, to read it without counting.

blocks.caption: Right hand, G position: thumb on G.
Left hand, G position: little finger on G.

blocks.text:
# If this happens
- **You play F, not F sharp.** The key signature means every F; look for it at the start of each line.
- **Tied notes get played twice.** Play the first, hold through the second.

**Until the next lesson:** chords and riff, each alone, each day.
